title: UK Director Liquidation, Part 1 of 3: The Real Process

scenes.label: HOOK
scenes.title: Hook
scenes.broll: Goal image, slow push-in. No figures on screen
scenes.vo: My company is coming to an end, and I'm closing it properly. If you're a UK director in the same spot, here's how a liquidation works, and the five things to do first.

scenes.label: INTRO
scenes.title: Part 1 of 3: the real process
scenes.vo: I'm Rifat, from Cambridge. This is Part 1 of three: the real process. It's time to say goodbye to this company, and doing the numbers is a hassle.
scenes.ph: Face cam placeholder · lower-third: Rifat · Cambridge, UK

scenes.label: CHAPTER 1
scenes.title: The goal
scenes.broll: Goal infographic, the three-step process highlighted
scenes.vo: Here's the goal. Company debt stays the company's. A licensed practitioner takes over, sells the assets and pays creditors in order. There's a lot of red tape in society, so understand it first.
overlay: 1 Hand over  →  2 Sell assets  →  3 Pay creditors in order
Lots of red tape: understand it first

scenes.label: CHAPTER 2
scenes.title: Five things to do first
scenes.broll: On-screen numbered list 1 to 5. Optional HMRC screen inset for step 1 (S2), UTR, login and balance hidden
scenes.vo: Five things to do first. Before anything else, understand what each one means, so you can actually process it. One: check your HMRC balance, so you know where you stand. Two: gather the company's books and records. Mine are in a storage unit. Three: get a licensed insolvency practitioner. I chose one with 4.8 stars on Trustpilot. Four: stop trading, and don't pay one creditor ahead of the others. Your practitioner will confirm this. Five: close your invoices and bring every bank account to zero, or the money goes to the Crown. I've recovered both outstanding customer invoices, and that's everything I received.
overlay: Understand each step, then process it
scenes.ph: Optional: HMRC screen (S2) inset for step 1. Blur UTR + login, hide the balance

scenes.label: CHAPTER 3
scenes.title: What it costs and how long it takes
scenes.broll: Cost and timeline graphic: £1,500 + £2,100, five stages, Gazette wait
scenes.vo: Here's what it costs, and how long it takes. A £1,500 deposit, then a £2,100 balance. I've paid both. Five stages run from the deposit to the banks at zero and the Gazette notice, then a wait of about two months. For me, creditors are notified on 19 November, and the proposed liquidation date is 2 December. Don't try to do this with AI alone. Learn the process, delegate the busywork to AI, and still use a professional.
overlay: Learn the process. Delegate with AI.
£1,500 deposit + £2,100 balance · about 2 months · liquidation 2 Dec

scenes.label: CHAPTER 4
scenes.title: The exceptions
scenes.broll: Four exception cards on screen, red accent
scenes.vo: Now the exceptions, because this matters. The protection isn't absolute. A director can still be personally liable for wrongful or fraudulent trading, personal guarantees, an overdrawn director's loan account, or paying one creditor first. Understand the basics, because even the people closest to you won't really get what you're doing, and they're not there with you. That's why the practitioner decides, not me.

scenes.label: CHAPTER 5
scenes.title: What my emails taught me
scenes.broll: Email timeline graphic (S12): chase reminders, the receipt, the liquidation-date email (names and addresses blurred)
scenes.vo: Three lessons from my own emails. One: the process stops until the balance is paid. My provider chased me six times, so don't leave it to the end. Two: answer everything in writing, and keep a list of what's still outstanding. Three: your records are part of the process, and the practitioner arranges the collection. And use AI to keep that list and make your life easier.
overlay: 2 Answer in writing, list what is outstanding
3 Records are part of the process
Use AI to make life easier

scenes.label: CHAPTER 6
scenes.title: How I keep track of it
scenes.broll: n8n canvas, 20 seconds (S3), then the dashboard (S10)
scenes.vo: I keep track of it all with an n8n workflow and a few AI agents: a planner, a risk checker and a director. But the real lesson is bigger. Learn from this company process, and build your own system and mindset for your next role.
overlay: n8n + AI agents: planner, risk checker, director
